patterns.title: target without its trailing dot
patterns.explain: In dnsconfig.js a CNAME or MX target needs a trailing dot, or dnscontrol reads it as a name inside your zone.

patterns.title: record name that already contains the zone
patterns.explain: Names in dnsconfig.js are relative to the zone, so A("www.studentXX.dojo.test", ...) becomes www.studentXX.dojo.test.studentXX.dojo.test.

patterns.title: the push to the shared zone was refused
patterns.section: 3. Try to go around the process
patterns.explain: dojo.test is the class's production zone. Only the DNS Apply CI job may change it, so a push from your terminal gets 403 on purpose.
patterns.fix: Nothing is broken. Make the change on a branch and open a pull request (Lab 3, step 4).

patterns.title: preview wants to delete a record you didn't write
patterns.section: 4. Make a change the proper way
patterns.explain: Your clone is behind main: a classmate's newer record is live, but not in your file, so preview shows it as a delete.
patterns.fix: git pull origin main (stash first if you haven't committed), then preview again: only your own CREATE should be left. Don't push until it is.

patterns.title: dnsconfig.js has a syntax error
patterns.explain: The file isn't valid JavaScript: usually a missing comma, quote or closing parenthesis near the line it names.
patterns.fix: Open the line named in the error and compare it with the lines around it. git diff shows exactly what you changed; git restore dnsconfig.js starts over.
